hoopR

The goal of hoopR is to provide tools for working with men’s basketball data.

It exports more than 1,300 functions:

  • NBA: the NBA Stats API (nba_*, about 200 functions), ESPN (espn_nba_*), the NBA G League (nbagl_*), Basketball-Reference (bref_*), RealGM (realgm_*), Fox Sports (fox_nba_*), official.nba.com officiating reports (nba_l2m(), nba_referee_assignments()), salary and mock-draft sources, and cross-source crosswalks.
  • Men’s college basketball: ESPN (espn_mbb_*), Ken Pomeroy’s kenpom.com (kp_*, for users with an active subscription), CollegeBasketballData (cbbd_*), Bart Torvik (torvik_*), the NCAA (ncaa_mbb_*) and Fox Sports (fox_mbb_*).
  • International: EuroLeague and EuroCup (euroleague_*) and about two dozen leagues and competitions, among them FIBA events (fiba_*), Spain’s ACB (acb_*), Italy’s LBA (lba_*), the VTB United League (vtb_*), Japan’s B.LEAGUE (bleague_*), Australia’s NBL (nbl_rosetta_*), Korea’s KBL (kbl_*) and China’s CBA (cba_*). See the function reference for the full list.
  • Loaders: load_nba_*(), load_mbb_*(), load_nba_stats_*() and load_ncaa_mbb_*() read pre-built play-by-play, box score, schedule, shot and model data from the sportsdataverse-data releases.

Data status

The load_*() functions read release assets on sportsdataverse-data. The badges below are rebuilt nightly from each producer’s latest workflow run and newest release files; idle means the sport is out of season. Full detail: sportsdataverse.org/status.

Installation

You can install the CRAN version of hoopR with:

install.packages("hoopR")

You can install the latest build from R-universe with:

install.packages("hoopR", repos = c("https://sportsdataverse.r-universe.dev", getOption("repos")))

You can install the development version of hoopR from GitHub with:

if (!requireNamespace("pak", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("sportsdataverse/hoopR")
# or, with remotes:
# if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("remotes")
# remotes::install_github("sportsdataverse/hoopR")

Quick start

NBA play-by-play for a season

load_nba_pbp() covers 2002-2027; pass several seasons (or seasons = 2002:2026) to load more at once.

nba_pbp <- hoopR::load_nba_pbp(seasons = 2026)
## 642472 rows of NBA play-by-play data from 1325 games.

Men’s college basketball play-by-play for a season

load_mbb_pbp() covers 2006-2027.

mbb_pbp <- hoopR::load_mbb_pbp(seasons = 2026)
## 2915731 rows of men's college basketball play-by-play data from 6275 games.

Companion packages

  • sdvplotR (0.3.0, pak::pak("sportsdataverse/sdvplotR")) adds team logos and colours to ggplot2 charts and draws shot charts from the hoopR shot loaders; see its NBA, men’s college and shot chart articles.
  • sportyR (2.4.5, install.packages("sportyR")) draws NBA, NCAA and FIBA courts to plot shot locations on.
  • wehoop is the women’s basketball companion (WNBA and women’s college basketball).
  • sportsdataverse-py is the Python package; most hoopR functions have a Python twin of the same name.

The SportsDataverse

hoopR is part of the SportsDataverse, a set of open-source packages for sports data.

Package Sport / Scope
cfbfastR College football
hoopR Men’s basketball (NBA and NCAA)
wehoop Women’s basketball (WNBA and NCAA)
fastRhockey Hockey (NHL and PWHL)
baseballr Baseball (MLB, MiLB, NCAA)
softballR College softball
oddsapiR Sports betting odds
recruitR College football recruiting
usfootballR US soccer
cfbseedR · cfb4th CFB playoff simulation · fourth-down decisions
cfbplotR · sdvplotR · sportyR Logos, colors, tables · playing surfaces
sportsdataverse-R Umbrella R metapackage
sportsdataverse-py · sportsdataverse.js Python and Node.js

See the full ecosystem at sportsdataverse.org.
